newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks fall on blue chip declines.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks fall on blue chip declines.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed down led by highly capitalised blue chips as investors kept to the sidelines to see how far the current round of profit-taking would go, brokers said.

The all share index closed five points down at 621.62. Falls outnumbered gains 31 to 11. Blue chips Aitken Spence fell three rupees to 100 on 100 shares, Commercial Bank 3.50 to 145.25 on 500 shares and Development Finance five to 270 on 100 shares.
"The small quantities on which these high cap blue chips fell smacks of someone trying to bring the index down in a hurry," said a broker who declined to be identified.
Turnover was 13.4 million rupees on 761,723 shares. The main trades were 165 Blue Diamonds Jewellery, 36,500 Grain Elevators, 14,500 Lanka Ceramic and 70,500 Lion Brewery.
Foreign buying was 7.5 million rupees and selling was 799,695 rupees.

"Turnover was low because buyers kept out to see where the index would settle," said Tivanka Ratnayake, a trader at brokerage John Keells. The index has been easing since profit-taking set in after the index rose four percent this year, brokers said.
